assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened a new platform where interaction-driven quantum phases are tunable by a gate and a twist angle. It is the clearest example of experiment surprising theory in a stable 2D material, and the continuum band-structure theory predicting the magic angle is quantitative and checkable against spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands and the magic angle (2011). Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 transport discovery. Andrei's group gave early STM evidence of flat bands and van Hove singularities. Credit is plausible for three but Bistritzer and others (e.g. Cao, Dean, Yacoby) have claims; I would choose theory plus the decisive experiment plus one early experimental pioneer.
assessment.maturity: Dozens of independent groups have reproduced the correlated states, with STM, transport and spectroscopy agreeing. Interpretation of the superconducting pairing is still debated, but the discovery itself is secure and the field is clearly timely.
uncertainties: Origin of superconductivity is unsettled
Fair split of credit among theory, transport and STM contributors, including Bistritzer and other early experimenters
Sample-to-sample twist-angle disorder complicates reproducibility

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators brought band topology into mainstream materials physics, with robust surface and edge states that are predicted and then directly measured. The concept is original, clear and has reshaped how materials are searched with first-principles theory.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical proposals. Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall edge channels in HgTe wells (2007) following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's prediction, and Hasan's group observed the 3D topological insulator surface states by ARPES. The package has more than three strong claimants (Mele, Zhang, Bernevig, Moore, Balents), so any three-person split leaves out defensible names. The credited names do not include Zhang.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent ARPES, transport and STM experiments, and by DFT predictions of materials that were then verified. Recognition is mature; the field has been honored in part via the Haldane/Thouless-Kosterlitz prize in 2016, which is context but not an obstacle.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases
Omission of Mele or of Zhang and collaborators may be contentious
Practical impact still limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the workhorse non-perturbative method for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions, and captures the Mott transition and heavy-fermion physics. Combined with DFT (DFT+DMFT) it gives quantitative, reproducible predictions for real materials, which is the kind of work I value.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt (1989) introduced the limit of large dimensions, Georges and Kotliar (1992) mapped it to an impurity problem, and Georges, Kotliar, Krauth and Rozenberg wrote the 1996 review. Metzner and Müller-Hartmann also have claims and Metzner is not in the supplied credit, so the proposed trio is the best available from the list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use, many successful applications and agreement with spectroscopy (photoemission, optics) for transition-metal oxides, plutonium and iron pnictides. Method is mature; it is a theoretical tool rather than a single discovered phenomenon, which some members may weigh against it.
uncertainties: A method rather than a discovery of a new phenomenon
Metzner's role is not representable
Accuracy of DMFT for low-dimensional systems is limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fractional charge and anyonic statistics are fundamentally new quantum behavior of particles in two dimensions, going beyond bosons and fermions. Observation in the quantum Hall regime links deep theory to measured devices, and anyon braiding underlies topological quantum computing ideas.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim (1977) introduced the theory of identical particles in low dimensions; Wilczek named anyons but is not in the supplied credit. Heiblum's shot-noise work measured fractional charge, and Fève and Manfra (with their groups) demonstrated braiding statistics in 2020. Three names can cover theory and fractional charge, but the braiding experiments may deserve recognition too; Laughlin, Tsui and Stormer are already honored for FQHE.
assessment.maturity: Fractional charge is well confirmed by several groups. Anyonic exchange statistics has been demonstrated in 2020 by two independent interferometer and collider experiments, but the evidence base is smaller and still developing, especially for non-Abelian anyons.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among theory, charge measurements and braiding experiments
Wilczek's absence from the credited names
Non-Abelian case remains unconfirmed

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum anomalous Hall effect gives quantized edge transport with no external magnetic field, a new state of matter realized in a magnetic topological insulator. It joins magnetism, topology and band structure, which is close to my own area, and is predicted by first-principles theory.
assessment.attribution: Fang, Dai and collaborators made the 2010 theoretical prediction for Cr/Fe-doped Bi2Se3 family (Yu et al., Science 2010), and Xue's group made the 2013 experimental observation. This is a clean theory-plus-experiment triple, though Haldane's 1988 model and other experimentalists (e.g. Chang, Moodera, Goldhaber-Gordon, Zhang) add overlap.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in several laboratories, though only at millikelvin temperatures and in a small number of materials; MnBi2Te4 expanded the platform. Interpretation is stable. Recognition is reasonably timely, but overlaps strongly with B001, so a joint prize might be a better fit.
uncertainties: Overlaps with topological insulator candidate
Very low temperature for quantization limits applications
Role of Chang and Moodera in the experimental credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism is a third class of collinear magnetic order, with zero net magnetization but spin-split bands, and is directly in the domain of electronic-structure theory of magnetism. It is conceptually clean and predicts spin-polarized currents without stray fields, with potential spintronic use.
assessment.attribution: Šmejkal, Jungwirth and Sinova formulated the symmetry classification and spin-group framework in 2022, building on earlier work on anisotropic spin-split bands. The three credited names are the natural group, but earlier related papers by others (e.g. Hayami, Yanagi, Kusunose; Yuan et al.) may complicate the story.
assessment.maturity: Recent: ARPES evidence in MnTe and CrSb (2024) and several transport and imaging experiments exist, but the independent confirmation is still maturing. As a committee member in magnetism I would see this as likely premature for now though promising.
uncertainties: Young field with limited independent confirmation
Prior related theory may complicate credit
Application impact not yet demonstrated

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of high-Tc superconductivity in MgB2 (39 K) and in iron pnictides (26 K up to 55 K) opened two new families of superconductors, and revived the multiband and unconventional pairing question. First-principles theory (DFT with electron-phonon calculations) described MgB2 quantitatively, which is a good example of predictive theory.
assessment.attribution: Akimitsu's group discovered MgB2 superconductivity in 2001 and Hosono's group discovered LaFeAsO(F) in 2008. These are two clear discoveries in separate families, so one prize combining them is a bit heterogeneous; two-name configuration is natural. No credited names need to be left out, though others contributed to the iron-based follow-up.
assessment.maturity: Both discoveries were rapidly confirmed by many groups worldwide. The mechanism of iron-based superconductors remains unsettled. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Compound discovery of two different families
Pairing mechanism in iron-based materials still unresolved
Whether the committee would split this into two separate recognitions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO junctions is the basis of read heads and MRAM, a direct application of quantum mechanical spin-dependent tunnelling with coherent Bloch-state filtering predicted by first-principles theory (Butler; Mathon and Umerski). It is practically important and the physics is quantitatively understood.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently observed room-temperature TMR in 1995, and Parkin and Yuasa reported giant TMR in MgO junctions in 2004. Butler, Zhang and colleagues made the key theoretical prediction but are not credited; Miyazaki also has a claim that could displace one of the three. Attribution is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature and widely deployed, and the physics is reproducibly confirmed, but the prize on spin electronics in 2007 for GMR partly overlaps and the advance can be seen as a refinement.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize
Theory contributors (Butler, Mathon) are not in the supplied credit
Miyazaki versus Parkin or Yuasa for the third place
